category: External References, Underlays, Point Clouds, Compare & Clipboard
description: Working with content that lives outside the drawing: the xref commands beyond XREF/XATTACH/XCLIP/XBIND (opening, in-place edit sessions, the command-line -XREF for scripts, the palette), raster image and PDF/DWF/DGN underlay attachment, clipping and adjustment, DGN import/export mapping, Navisworks coordination models, point clouds, geographic location and online maps, DWG Compare and Xref Compare, ARCHIVE for sheet sets, OLE objects, hyperlinks and the Windows clipboard commands that move geometry between drawings.

tools.name: -XREF
tools.description: Command-line version of XREF for scripts and macros. It exposes every operation of the External References palette as a keyword: attach or overlay a file, bind it into the drawing (as a block or with Insert semantics via BINDTYPE), detach, reload, unload, list, and repath. Because it never opens the palette it is the way batch processes fix broken xref paths or bind drawings for issue.
tools.usage:
-XREF
Enter an option [?/Bind/Detach/Path/Unload/Reload/Overlay/Attach] <Attach>:
Attach:  Enter name of file to attach: <path>  then insertion point / scale / rotation prompts (as -INSERT)
Path:    Edit xref name(s): <name or wildcard>   Enter new path: <path>
Bind:    Enter xref name(s) to bind: <name or *>
Reload:  Enter xref name(s) to reload: *

parameters.name: Attach / Overlay
parameters.description: Attach nests the xref into any drawing that later references this one; Overlay does not. XREFTYPE sets the default.

parameters.name: Bind
parameters.description: Convert the xref into a local block; BINDTYPE 0 keeps renamed dependent symbols (Bind style, SITE$0$WALL), 1 merges them (Insert style, WALL).

parameters.name: Detach / Unload / Reload
parameters.description: Remove the reference entirely, keep it defined but not displayed, or re-read the file from disk.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Change the stored path of one or several xrefs; REFPATHTYPE decides full/relative/no-path for new attachments.
List xrefs with their paths and status.

tools.example:
; Script: repath every xref to a new project folder and bind for issue
-XREF
P
*
C:/proj/1042/xrefs/*.dwg
-XREF
R
*
BINDTYPE
1
-XREF
B
*

; AutoLISP overlay with insertion at origin
(command "_.-XREF" "_O" "C:/proj/SITE.dwg" '(0 0 0) 1 1 0)
tools.notes: FILEDIA must be 0 or the Attach option opens a file dialog. The Path option cannot change a relative path to absolute unless the file is found; use the palette or (vla-put-Path) if you need to set an unresolvable path. Binding with BINDTYPE 1 can silently merge layers of the same name.

tools.name: EXTERNALREFERENCES
tools.description: Opens the External References palette that lists every attached DWG xref, raster image, PDF/DWF/DGN underlay, point cloud and coordination model with its status (Loaded, Unloaded, Not Found, Needs reloading), size, type, date and saved path. Right-click commands cover Attach, Open, Reload, Unload, Detach, Bind and Select New Path / Find and Replace path, and the Details/Preview pane shows the found path versus the saved path, which is what you check when a reference is unresolved. XREF and ER open the same palette; EXTERNALREFERENCESCLOSE closes it.
tools.usage:
EXTERNALREFERENCES  (alias ER, XR / XREF; Insert tab > Reference panel > dialog launcher)
EXTERNALREFERENCESCLOSE

parameters.name: Attach drop-down
parameters.description: Attach DWG, Image, DWF, DGN, PDF, Point Cloud, Coordination Model - each goes to the matching *ATTACH command.

parameters.name: Change Path Type
parameters.description: Switch a reference between Absolute, Relative and No Path (relative paths need the host drawing to be saved).

parameters.name: Find and Replace
parameters.description: Replace a substring in the saved paths of all selected references - the bulk repath tool.

parameters.name: Status column
parameters.description: Loaded, Unloaded, Not Found, Unreferenced, Orphaned (parent xref missing), Unresolved.

parameters.name: XREFNOTIFY
parameters.description: 0 no notification, 1 balloon when an xref changes on disk, 2 balloon plus icon in the status bar.

tools.example:
EXTERNALREFERENCES
(select the Not Found rows, right-click > Select New Path, browse to the moved folder; all siblings in the same folder are repathed together)
tools.notes: The palette works per drawing; use ETRANSMIT or a REFPATHTYPE-relative convention to keep sets portable. The ActiveX/.NET equivalents are Database.GetXrefGraph / vla-get-Path on the block definition, and the (vla-Reload) method.

tools.name: CLASSICXREF
tools.description: Opens the legacy Xref Manager dialog (pre-2007 modal interface) instead of the External References palette. Some users and older macros prefer its list/tree view with Attach, Detach, Reload, Unload, Bind and Open buttons all visible at once. It manages DWG xrefs only - images and underlays appear only in the palette.
tools.usage: CLASSICXREF  (modal Xref Manager dialog)

parameters.name: List View / Tree View
parameters.description: Flat list or nesting hierarchy of xrefs.

parameters.name: Xref Found At / Saved Path
parameters.description: Edit the saved path or browse for the file.

tools.example:
CLASSICXREF
(select SITE, click Bind, choose Insert, OK)
tools.notes: Kept for compatibility; new work should use EXTERNALREFERENCES or -XREF. CLASSICIMAGE is the matching legacy Image Manager.

tools.name: XOPEN
tools.description: Opens the source drawing of a selected xref in a new drawing window for editing, without hunting for the file in Explorer. Save it, switch back to the host and reload the xref (or let XREFNOTIFY prompt you). Compared with REFEDIT it edits the whole file with all commands available, which is safer for anything beyond a small fix.
tools.usage:
XOPEN
Select xref: <pick any object of the xref>
tools.example:
XOPEN
(click the site plan xref; SITE.dwg opens in a new tab)
(edit, QSAVE, Ctrl+Tab back to the host)
-XREF R SITE
tools.notes: Nested xrefs open the file that contains the picked object. The file opens read-only if another user has it locked (.dwl file present). Also available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: REFCLOSE
tools.description: Ends an in-place reference editing session started with REFEDIT, either saving the changes back to the xref file or block definition or discarding them. Until REFCLOSE runs, the rest of the drawing is faded (XFADECTL) and most file commands are disabled, so scripts that call REFEDIT must always finish with REFCLOSE.
tools.usage:
REFCLOSE
Enter option [Save/Discard reference changes] <Save>:

parameters.name: Save
parameters.description: Write the working set back to the block definition, or to the xref file on disk (the file is saved immediately).

parameters.name: Discard
parameters.description: Abandon the changes; the working set objects return to their original state.

parameters.name: REFEDITNAME
parameters.description: Read-only variable holding the name of the reference being edited (empty when none) - test it before starting another session.

tools.example:
REFEDIT
(pick the block, OK)
(modify geometry)
REFCLOSE
S

; guard in LISP
(if (/= "" (getvar "REFEDITNAME")) (command "_.REFCLOSE" "_S"))
tools.notes: Saving to an xref file overwrites that file even if other users have it open. XEDIT set to 0 in the xref's own drawing blocks in-place editing of it from any host.

tools.name: REFSET
tools.description: Adds objects to or removes objects from the working set during an in-place reference edit (REFEDIT). Objects added become part of the block or xref when REFCLOSE saves; objects removed are left in the host drawing. Use it when new geometry drawn during the session should live in the reference, or when something must be pulled out of a block.
tools.usage:
REFSET
Transfer objects between the RefEdit working set and host drawing...
Enter an option [Add/Remove] <Add>:
Select objects: <selection>

parameters.name: Add
parameters.description: Move host objects into the working set (they will be saved into the reference).

parameters.name: Remove
parameters.description: Move working-set objects out to the host drawing.

tools.example:
REFEDIT (pick the DOOR block)
(draw a swing arc)
REFSET
A
(select the arc) Enter
REFCLOSE S
tools.notes: Objects drawn while the session is active are added to the working set automatically; REFSET is for pre-existing objects. Only available between REFEDIT and REFCLOSE.

tools.name: XCOMPARE
tools.description: Xref Compare (2021+). Compares an attached xref with the current state of its source file (or with another DWG) and highlights the differences directly in the host drawing: objects only in the old version in one colour, only in the new version in another, unchanged geometry dimmed, each change set wrapped in a revision cloud. A toolbar steps through the change sets (XCOMPARERCNEXT / XCOMPARERCPREV) and XCOMPARECLOSE ends the comparison. AutoCAD can also trigger it automatically when it notices the xref changed on disk (XCOMPAREENABLE).
tools.usage:
XCOMPARE
Select xref to compare: <pick>
(Xref Compare toolbar: settings, previous/next change set, show/hide old/new/common objects, Close)
XCOMPARERCNEXT / XCOMPARERCPREV / XCOMPARECLOSE

parameters.name: Compare with
parameters.description: The referenced file's newest saved version, or Browse to any other DWG.

parameters.name: XCOMPAREENABLE
parameters.description: 1 (default) lets the xref-changed notification offer Compare; 0 disables Xref Compare.

parameters.name: XCOMPARECOLORMODE
parameters.description: 0 keeps host colours, 1 dims the host drawing during the comparison.

parameters.name: XCOMPAREBAKPATH / XCOMPAREBAKSIZE
parameters.description: Where the backup copies used for comparison are kept and how large the folder may grow.

parameters.name: COMPARESHOWCONTEXT
parameters.description: Whether objects not part of the comparison stay visible.

tools.example:
XCOMPARE
(pick the architectural background xref)
(step through change sets with the toolbar arrows, then Close)
-XREF R A-BACKGROUND
tools.notes: Xref Compare does not modify either file; reload the xref afterwards to see the new version normally. Not available in the Core Console. DWG Compare (COMPARE) is the whole-drawing equivalent that can also import objects.

tools.name: COMPARE
tools.description: DWG Compare (2019+). Compares the current drawing with another DWG and shows the result in the current drawing: objects only in the current drawing in green, objects only in the other file in red, common objects in grey, differences grouped into change sets outlined by revision clouds. Since 2020 the comparison runs in the current drawing (not a third file), so you can edit while it is active, import objects from the other file (COMPAREIMPORT) or export a snapshot (COMPAREEXPORT). -COMPARE is the command-line form.
tools.usage:
COMPARE
(Select the drawing to compare: file dialog)
(DWG Compare toolbar: Settings, previous/next change set, import objects, export snapshot, Exit compare)
-COMPARE
Enter the file name to compare with: <path>
COMPARECLOSE  ends the comparison

parameters.name: Settings gear
parameters.description: Toggle display of objects only in drawing 1, only in drawing 2, common objects, revision clouds; change colours (COMPARECOLOR1/2/COMMON), cloud shape/margin (COMPARERCSHAPE, COMPARERCMARGIN), filters for hatches, text and properties (COMPAREHATCH, COMPARETEXT, COMPAREPROPS) and tolerance (COMPARETOLERANCE).

parameters.name: COMPARESHOW1 / COMPARESHOW2 / COMPARESHOWCOMMON / COMPARESHOWRC
parameters.description: System variables behind the display toggles.

parameters.name: COMPAREFRONT
parameters.description: Which drawing's objects draw on top where they overlap.

tools.example:
-COMPARE
C:/proj/issue_02/PLAN.dwg
(review change sets with the toolbar arrows)
COMPAREIMPORT
(select the red objects to bring into the current drawing) Enter
COMPARECLOSE
tools.notes: Only model space is compared; layouts, xref content and OLE objects are ignored. Compare respects layer visibility at the time it starts, so thaw everything first. The AutoCAD web app has the same feature under Compare.

tools.name: COMPAREIMPORT
tools.description: During an active DWG Compare, copies selected objects that exist only in the compared (second) drawing into the current drawing, effectively merging changes from another revision one object at a time. The imported objects lose their compare colouring and become normal objects on their original layers, which are created if missing.
tools.usage:
COMPAREIMPORT
Select objects to import: <pick red objects from the compared drawing> Enter

parameters.name: selection
parameters.description: Only objects flagged 'in the compared drawing only' are eligible; common or current-only objects are ignored.

tools.example:
COMPARE (choose the consultant's revised file)
COMPAREIMPORT
(select the new column grid lines) Enter
COMPARECLOSE
QSAVE
tools.notes: Available from 2020; before that, compare produced a separate result drawing and copy/paste was the only merge route. Imported objects keep the other drawing's properties, including layers that may not follow your standards - run CHECKSTANDARDS afterwards.

tools.name: COMPAREEXPORT
tools.description: During an active DWG Compare, writes the comparison result to a new 'snapshot' drawing: a DWG containing the differences with their compare colours, revision clouds and a summary, suitable for sending to someone who does not have both revisions. The snapshot is a normal drawing that can be plotted or published.
tools.usage:
COMPAREEXPORT
(Save As dialog: snapshot drawing name)

parameters.name: snapshot file
parameters.description: New DWG; the current comparison settings (visible object classes, colours) determine its content.

tools.example:
COMPARE (choose the previous issue)
COMPAREEXPORT -> C:\proj\PLAN_compare_02_vs_03.dwg
COMPARECLOSE
tools.notes: The snapshot is static; rerun COMPARE and export again after further edits. COMPAREINFO is the lightweight alternative that only inserts the comparison metadata as text or copies it to the clipboard.

tools.name: COMPAREINFO
tools.description: Inserts or copies the properties of the two drawings in an active DWG Compare - file names, paths, last-saved dates and who saved them - as a block of MTEXT in the drawing or as text on the clipboard. Used to stamp a compare snapshot or a review sheet with the provenance of the comparison.
tools.usage:
COMPAREINFO
Enter an option [Insert/Copy] <Insert>:
Insert: Specify insertion point: <point>

parameters.name: Insert
parameters.description: Place the information as multiline text in the current drawing.

parameters.name: Copy
parameters.description: Put the same text on the Windows clipboard.

tools.example:
COMPAREINFO
I
(click in an empty area of the layout)
tools.notes: Only works while COMPARE is active. The text is plain MTEXT, not fields, so it does not update.

tools.name: IMAGECLIP
tools.description: Clips the display of an attached raster image to a rectangular or polygonal boundary, or inverts the clip to hide the inside. The image data is untouched; only the displayed region changes, and the boundary can be edited with grips or removed later. IMAGEFRAME / FRAME control whether the clip boundary is drawn and plotted.
tools.usage:
IMAGECLIP
Select image to clip: <pick image edge>
Enter image clipping option [ON/OFF/Delete/New boundary] <New>:
New boundary: [Select polyline/Polygonal/Rectangular/Invert clip] <Rectangular>:

parameters.name: ON / OFF
parameters.description: Toggle the existing clip without deleting it.

parameters.name: Delete
parameters.description: Remove the boundary and show the whole image.

parameters.name: New boundary
parameters.description: Rectangle by two corners, polygon by points, or an existing closed polyline; Invert clip hides the inside instead of the outside.

parameters.name: IMAGEFRAME
parameters.description: 0 frame not shown or plotted, 1 shown and plotted, 2 shown but not plotted.

tools.example:
IMAGECLIP
(pick the aerial image)
N
P
(pick the site boundary points) Enter
IMAGEFRAME
2
tools.notes: Selecting an image requires clicking its frame unless IMAGEFRAME is 0 - then use a crossing window or (ssget "_X" '((0 . "IMAGE"))). Clipped images still load the whole file, so crop large scans externally if performance matters.

tools.name: IMAGEADJUST
tools.description: Adjusts brightness, contrast and fade of a raster image without touching the source file - the standard way to grey out a scanned background so new linework reads over it. -IMAGEADJUST takes the three values at the command line. IMAGEQUALITY switches between High (full resolution) and Draft (faster) display for all images, and TRANSPARENCY makes the background colour of bitonal images see-through.
tools.usage:
IMAGEADJUST
Select image(s): <pick>
(Image Adjust dialog: Brightness 0-100, Contrast 0-100, Fade 0-100, Reset)
-IMAGEADJUST: prompts for the three values
IMAGEQUALITY  Enter image quality setting [High/Draft] <High>:
TRANSPARENCY  Select image(s): ... Enter transparency mode [ON/OFF] <OFF>:

parameters.name: Brightness
parameters.description: 0 dark to 100 light; default 50.

parameters.name: Contrast
parameters.description: 0 flat to 100 hard; default 50.

parameters.name: Fade
parameters.description: 0 opaque to 100 blended into the background colour; 50-70 is typical for a reference scan.

parameters.name: TRANSPARENCY
parameters.description: Only bitonal (1-bit) and images with an alpha channel support it; the background pixels become transparent.

tools.example:
-IMAGEADJUST
(pick the scanned plan)
50
50
70
TRANSPARENCY
(pick it again)
ON
tools.notes: Fade applies to the image's display only; plots use the same values so a 70 fade prints light grey. The Properties palette exposes the same three values for multi-image edits.

tools.name: FRAME
tools.description: Master switch for the display and plotting of the frames of every reference type at once - images, PDF/DWF/DGN underlays, clipped xrefs, wipeouts and point clouds. Setting FRAME writes the same value into IMAGEFRAME, PDFFRAME, DWFFRAME, DGNFRAME, XCLIPFRAME, WIPEOUTFRAME and POINTCLOUDCLIPFRAME; reading it returns 3 when those individual variables disagree.
tools.usage:
FRAME = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3
0 frames hidden and not plotted
1 frames displayed and plotted
2 frames displayed but not plotted (usual working setting)
3 (read-only) individual frame variables are set to different values

parameters.name: IMAGEFRAME / PDFFRAME / DWFFRAME / DGNFRAME
parameters.description: Per-type variables with the same 0/1/2 meaning.

parameters.name: XCLIPFRAME
parameters.description: Frame of clipped xrefs and blocks.

parameters.name: WIPEOUTFRAME
parameters.description: Frame of WIPEOUT objects (2013+; before that WIPEOUT's own Frames option).

parameters.name: POINTCLOUDCLIPFRAME
parameters.description: Crop boundary frame of point clouds.

tools.example:
; Script prelude for plotting: show frames on screen but keep them off paper
FRAME 2

; AutoLISP
(setvar "FRAME" 2)
tools.notes: With frames at 0 an image or underlay can only be selected by a crossing window or by name (Properties / ssget filters), not by clicking. Saved in the drawing.

tools.name: PDFCLIP
tools.description: Clips a PDF underlay to a rectangular or polygonal boundary so only the relevant part of a multi-sheet or oversized PDF is displayed and plotted; Invert clip hides the inside. Works exactly like IMAGECLIP and DWFCLIP/DGNCLIP, with PDFFRAME governing the boundary's visibility.
tools.usage:
PDFCLIP
Select PDF underlay to clip: <pick>
Enter PDF clipping option [ON/OFF/Delete/New boundary] <New boundary>:
[Select polyline/Polygonal/Rectangular/Invert clip] <Rectangular>:

parameters.name: ON / OFF / Delete / New boundary
parameters.description: As IMAGECLIP.

parameters.name: PDFFRAME
parameters.description: 0 hidden, 1 shown and plotted, 2 shown not plotted.

tools.example:
PDFCLIP
(pick the underlay)
N
R
(two corners around the detail you need)
tools.notes: Clipping does not change which page is displayed - that is the Page Number property of the underlay. PDFLAYERS controls layer visibility inside the PDF; PDFOSNAP (or the underlay's Snap property) allows snapping to its vectors.

tools.name: PDFLAYERS
tools.description: Opens the Underlay Layers dialog for a PDF underlay that carries layer information (PDFs produced by AutoCAD with 'Include layer information' or by other CAD tools), letting you turn individual PDF layers on or off in the underlay's display. The equivalent commands for other formats are DWFLAYERS and DGNLAYERS; ULAYERS is the generic one that works on any underlay type.
tools.usage:
PDFLAYERS
Select PDF underlay: <pick>
(Underlay Layers dialog: On/Off checkbox per layer, search field)
ULAYERS  (any underlay type)

parameters.name: Layer list
parameters.description: PDF optional content groups; toggling affects the display of this underlay only, not the file.

tools.example:
PDFLAYERS
(pick the underlay, uncheck the DIMENSIONS and TEXT layers, OK)
tools.notes: Layer states are saved in the drawing per underlay. PDFs without optional content show a single unnamed layer. Settings are also available from the contextual PDF Underlay ribbon tab (Edit Layers).

tools.name: PDFSHXTEXT
tools.description: Recognise Text (2017.1+). PDFIMPORT converts TrueType text to MTEXT but text that was plotted with SHX fonts arrives as geometry (lines and arcs); PDFSHXTEXT compares that geometry against the SHX fonts installed and turns matching clusters into MTEXT objects, so scanned-in dimensions and notes become editable. -PDFSHXTEXT is the command-line form; PDFSHXTHRESHOLD, PDFSHXBESTFONT and PDFSHXLAYER tune the recognition.
tools.usage:
PDFSHXTEXT
(PDF Text Recognition Settings dialog: fonts to compare against, threshold)
Select objects: <the imported SHX geometry> Enter
-PDFSHXTEXT: Select objects, then compares using the current settings

parameters.name: Fonts list
parameters.description: SHX fonts to try (romans.shx, simplex.shx, txt.shx...); the fewer, the faster.

parameters.name: PDFSHXTHRESHOLD
parameters.description: Percentage (default 95) of the geometry that must match a font before it is converted; lower for degraded PDFs.

parameters.name: PDFSHXBESTFONT
parameters.description: 1 keep testing all fonts and use the best match, 0 stop at the first font above the threshold.

parameters.name: PDFSHXLAYER
parameters.description: Layer for the new text: 0 current layer, 1 same layer as the geometry, 2 layer named PDF_Text.

parameters.name: PDFSHX (export side)
parameters.description: 1 stores SHX text as hidden comments in PDFs plotted from AutoCAD so the round trip works without recognition.

tools.example:
PDFIMPORT (choose the drawing PDF)
PDFSHXTEXT
(tick romans.shx and simplex.shx, threshold 90, OK)
(select the text-like geometry) Enter
-> 'Converted 212 objects to 48 MTEXT objects'
tools.notes: Works only on geometry, not on raster images (use OCR outside AutoCAD for scans). Combining recognised text into paragraphs afterwards is done with TXT2MTXT. Not available in AutoCAD LT before 2018.

tools.name: DGNATTACH
tools.description: Attaches a MicroStation V7 or V8 DGN file as an underlay - a lightweight, non-editable reference that displays the DGN's design model or a sheet model, can be clipped (DGNCLIP), have its levels toggled (DGNLAYERS) and be snapped to. Choose this over DGNIMPORT when the MicroStation file is a background you do not need to edit. -DGNATTACH is the command-line form.
tools.usage:
DGNATTACH
(Select DGN File dialog, then Attach DGN Underlay dialog: model to attach, conversion units Master/Sub, path type, insertion point / scale / rotation)
-DGNATTACH
Path to DGN file to attach: <path>
Enter name of model or [?] <Default>:
Specify conversion units [Master/Sub] <Master>:
Specify insertion point: ...

parameters.name: Model
parameters.description: A V8 DGN can hold several design/sheet models; one underlay shows one model.

parameters.name: Conversion units
parameters.description: Whether the DGN master units or sub units map to one drawing unit.

parameters.name: DGNFRAME / DGNOSNAP
parameters.description: Frame display and whether object snaps see the underlay's geometry.

tools.example:
-DGNATTACH
C:/proj/survey.dgn
Default
M
0,0
1
0
tools.notes: Underlays are listed in the External References palette. Text and dimension appearance depends on the DGN's font resources; missing fonts are substituted. The Core Console supports DGN attach and import.

tools.name: DGNIMPORT
tools.description: Imports a MicroStation DGN (V7/V8) file into a new or the current drawing, translating levels to layers, cells to blocks, line styles to linetypes, text and dimensions to AutoCAD objects. A mapping setup (DGNMAPPING) controls how levels, linetypes, lineweights and colours are renamed. Use DGNIMPORT when the geometry must be edited natively; use DGNATTACH when it is only a background.
tools.usage:
DGNIMPORT
(Import DGN Settings dialog: design model to import, external DGN references (ignore/translate/attach as underlay), explode text nodes, conversion units, mapping setup)
-DGNIMPORT: command-line prompts for file, model, units and mapping setup name

parameters.name: Design model to import
parameters.description: Which model of a V8 file becomes model space (sheet models become layouts).

parameters.name: External DGN references
parameters.description: Ignore, Translate references to blocks, or Create DGN underlays for them.

parameters.name: Explode text node to text elements
parameters.description: Break multi-line text nodes into single-line text objects.

parameters.name: Mapping setup
parameters.description: A named translation table from DGNMAPPING (Standard is the default).

parameters.name: DGNIMPORTMAX / DGNIMPORTMODE
parameters.description: Limit on element count and import-into-current vs new drawing behaviour.

tools.example:
DGNMAPPING (create setup 'CIVIL': level Road_CL -> layer C-ROAD-CNTR, line style 3 -> CENTER)
DGNIMPORT
(select survey.dgn, model Default, units Master, mapping CIVIL, OK)
tools.notes: Complex elements (B-spline surfaces, cells with shared cell definitions) may arrive as proxies or be dropped; check the import log on the text screen. AutoCAD LT supports DGN import/attach since 2019.

tools.name: DGNEXPORT
tools.description: Exports the current drawing (model space or a layout) to a MicroStation V8 or V7 DGN file. A seed file supplies the DGN's units, working resolution and global origin, and a DGNMAPPING setup decides how layers become levels, linetypes become line styles and lineweights/colours are translated. Xrefs can be bound or written as DGN references.
tools.usage:
DGNEXPORT
(Export DGN Settings dialog: external DWG references (bind/create references/ignore), DWG underlays, seed file, master/sub units, mapping setup)
-DGNEXPORT: command-line prompts including the seed file path and mapping setup

parameters.name: Seed file
parameters.description: A V8 or V7 .dgn whose settings the export inherits; AutoCAD ships imperial and metric seed files in the Support folder.

parameters.name: External DWG references
parameters.description: Translate all DWG references to DGN files, Bind them into one DGN, or Ignore.

parameters.name: Mapping setup
parameters.description: DGNMAPPING translation table.

parameters.name: Conversion units
parameters.description: One drawing unit equals one Master unit or one Sub unit of the seed.

tools.example:
-DGNEXPORT
C:/out/PLAN.dgn
V8
C:/Program Files/Autodesk/AutoCAD 2025/Support/V8-Metric-Seed3D.dgn
M
Standard
tools.notes: AutoCAD object types without a DGN equivalent (tables, MLEADERs, fields) are exported as their visual geometry. EXPORT with the .dgn extension calls the same routine. Verify the result in MicroStation or Bentley View because line style scaling often needs adjusting.

tools.name: DGNMAPPING
tools.description: Opens the DGN Mapping Setups dialog to create, edit, rename and delete named translation tables used by DGNIMPORT and DGNEXPORT. A setup has four tabs - Layers/Levels, Linetypes/Line styles, Lineweights/Weights and Colors - mapping each AutoCAD property to its DGN counterpart and back. Setups are stored in the user's dgnsetups.ini so they can be shared across projects.
tools.usage:
DGNMAPPING
(dialog: New / Rename / Modify / Delete setups; per-setup tabs with DWG-to-DGN and DGN-to-DWG columns)

parameters.name: Layer mapping
parameters.description: Layer name -> level name (and number) and the reverse; unmapped layers are created with the same name.

parameters.name: Linetype mapping
parameters.description: AutoCAD linetype -> DGN line style number or custom style name.

parameters.name: Lineweight and colour mapping
parameters.description: mm lineweights to DGN weight 0-31; ACI colours to DGN colour table indices.

parameters.name: DGNMAPPINGPATH
parameters.description: System variable holding the folder of dgnsetups.ini.

tools.example:
DGNMAPPING
(New: 'CLIENT_X'; Layers tab: A-WALL -> Walls, A-DOOR -> Doors; Colors tab: 1 -> 3; OK)
DGNEXPORT (choose CLIENT_X as mapping setup)
tools.notes: Mappings are by exact name; wildcards are not supported. Keep the .ini under version control when several users must export identically.

tools.name: DWFATTACH
tools.description: Attaches a DWF or DWFx file as an underlay, choosing which sheet of a multi-sheet DWF to show. The underlay behaves like a PDF underlay: it can be clipped (DWFCLIP), have layers toggled (DWFLAYERS), be snapped to (DWFOSNAP) and adjusted for fade/contrast/monochrome (ADJUST). It is the reference counterpart of publishing to DWF with PUBLISH or EXPORTDWF. -DWFATTACH is the command-line form.
tools.usage:
DWFATTACH
(Select DWF file, then Attach DWF Underlay dialog: sheet, path type, insertion point / scale / rotation)
-DWFATTACH
Path to DWF or DWFx file to attach: <path>
Enter name of sheet or [?] <first sheet>:
Specify insertion point: ...
DWFCLIP / DWFLAYERS / ADJUST for clipping, layers, fade and contrast

parameters.name: Sheet
parameters.description: The DWF sheet (layout) to display; each underlay object shows one sheet.

parameters.name: DWFFRAME / DWFOSNAP
parameters.description: Frame display and snapping to underlay vectors.

parameters.name: ADJUST
parameters.description: Generic underlay adjust command: Fade, Contrast, Monochrome for DWF, DGN and PDF underlays.

tools.example:
-DWFATTACH
C:/issue/SET_03.dwfx
A-101 PLAN
0,0
1
0
ADJUST (pick it) F 60 C 50 M Y
tools.notes: DWF underlays are vector, so zooming stays sharp, but 3D DWF content shows as a 2D projection. Markups stored in a DWF are handled separately by OPENDWFMARKUP / the Markup Set Manager, not by DWFATTACH.

tools.name: CMATTACH
tools.description: Coordination model attach (2016+): inserts a reference to a Navisworks NWD or NWC file (and Autodesk Docs / BIM 360 coordination models) so a federated 3D model can be displayed as a faded, snappable background while you draft in AutoCAD. COORDINATIONMODELATTACH is the long form. The model is view-only; CMFADECOLOR and CMFADEOPACITY control how strongly it is dimmed and CMOSNAP whether object snaps see its geometry.
tools.usage:
CMATTACH
(Select Coordination Model dialog: .nwd/.nwc file; insertion point, scale, rotation, path type)
-CMATTACH: command-line prompts

parameters.name: CMFADECOLOR
parameters.description: 0-90, amount of black blended into the model's colours.

parameters.name: CMFADEOPACITY
parameters.description: 0-90, transparency applied to the model.

parameters.name: CMOSNAP
parameters.description: 1 lets object snaps acquire coordination model vertices and edges.

tools.example:
CMATTACH
(choose Structure.nwd, insertion 0,0,0, scale 1, OK)
CMOSNAP 1
(draw the pipe route snapping to the steel model)
tools.notes: Requires a 64-bit AutoCAD with hardware acceleration; not available in AutoCAD LT or the Core Console. The model is listed in the External References palette and can be reloaded when the NWD is republished.

tools.name: POINTCLOUDATTACH
tools.description: Attaches a point cloud project (.rcp) or scan (.rcs) produced by Autodesk ReCap as a reference object that displays millions of points with level-of-detail streaming. Once attached, the Point Cloud contextual ribbon offers stylisation (POINTCLOUDSTYLIZE: scan colour, elevation, intensity, classification), cropping (POINTCLOUDCROP), section planes and 2D geometry extraction (PCEXTRACTSECTION, PCEXTRACTCENTERLINE, PCEXTRACTCORNER, PCEXTRACTEDGE). -POINTCLOUDATTACH is the command-line form.
tools.usage:
POINTCLOUDATTACH
(Select Point Cloud File: .rcp / .rcs; Attach Point Cloud dialog: path type, insertion point, scale, rotation, Use geographic location, Lock point cloud)
-POINTCLOUDATTACH
Path to point cloud file to attach: <path>
Specify insertion point [Geographic]: ...

parameters.name: Use geographic location
parameters.description: Place the cloud by its georeferencing if the drawing has a GEOGRAPHICLOCATION.

parameters.name: Lock point cloud
parameters.description: Prevent accidental moving (also the Lock property).

parameters.name: POINTCLOUDPOINTMAX / POINTCLOUDLOD / POINTCLOUDPOINTSIZE
parameters.description: Display budget (points on screen), level of detail 1-10 and point size in pixels.

parameters.name: POINTCLOUDCACHESIZE
parameters.description: Memory reserved for point cloud display, in hundreds of MB.

tools.example:
-POINTCLOUDATTACH
C:/scans/Building.rcp
0,0,0
1
0
POINTCLOUDSTYLIZE (choose Elevation)
POINTCLOUDCROP (pick cloud) R (two corners) I(nside)
tools.notes: Raw .las/.e57/.pts files must first be indexed in ReCap (the RECAP command launches it). Point clouds need a 64-bit AutoCAD with a capable GPU; AutoCAD LT can display but not attach them. The Point Cloud Manager (POINTCLOUDMANAGER) toggles individual scans and regions.

tools.name: POINTCLOUDCROP
tools.description: Crops a point cloud to a rectangular, polygonal or circular boundary drawn in the current view, keeping either the inside or the outside; crops can be stacked, toggled, saved as named crop states (POINTCLOUDCROPSTATE) and removed with POINTCLOUDUNCROP. Cropping is a display filter - the .rcp file is not modified - and it is the usual first step before extracting sections or centrelines.
tools.usage:
POINTCLOUDCROP
Select point cloud: <pick>
[Rectangular/Polygonal/Circular] <Rectangular>:
(specify the boundary)
[Inside/Outside] <Inside>:
POINTCLOUDUNCROP  removes all crops from the selected cloud
POINTCLOUDCROPSTATE  Save / Restore / Delete named crop states

parameters.name: Inside / Outside
parameters.description: Keep points inside the boundary, or remove them.

parameters.name: Crop planes
parameters.description: Boundaries are extruded perpendicular to the current view, so set the view (PLAN, front, UCS) before cropping.

parameters.name: POINTCLOUDCLIPFRAME
parameters.description: Show or hide the crop boundary lines.

tools.example:
PLAN
POINTCLOUDCROP
(pick cloud)
P
(trace the floor plate outline) Enter
I
POINTCLOUDCROPSTATE S LEVEL2
tools.notes: Each crop is applied to the whole cloud object; to show two separate areas use the Point Cloud Manager regions or two attachments. Cropped-away points are not selectable by object snaps.

tools.name: PCEXTRACTSECTION
tools.description: Generates 2D line geometry from a section through a point cloud: with a section plane (SECTIONPLANE) or a horizontal slice defined during the command, the points within the slice thickness are fitted with lines or polylines that approximate walls, columns and other planar features. Related extraction commands are PCEXTRACTCENTERLINE (axis of a cylindrical pipe segment), PCEXTRACTEDGE (line at the intersection of two planes) and PCEXTRACTCORNER (point at the intersection of three planes).
tools.usage:
PCEXTRACTSECTION
Select a section object or [Point cloud]: <pick section plane> | P then pick cloud and define elevation/thickness
(Extract Section Lines from Point Cloud dialog: extraction type Full/Optimal, output Lines or Polylines, Layer, Color, Linetype, Width, Min segment length, tolerance, Draw in current drawing / Create new drawing)
PCEXTRACTCENTERLINE  Select point cloud segment: (click a pipe)
PCEXTRACTEDGE / PCEXTRACTCORNER  click adjacent planar segments

parameters.name: Slice thickness
parameters.description: Distance either side of the section plane whose points are considered.

parameters.name: Optimal extraction
parameters.description: Simplified 2D lines with fewer segments; Full keeps more detail.

parameters.name: Minimum segment length / tolerance
parameters.description: Noise filters; raise them for scans with heavy clutter.

parameters.name: Point cloud segmentation
parameters.description: Centreline/edge/corner extraction needs an .rcp that ReCap segmented into planes and cylinders.

tools.example:
SECTIONPLANE (draw a horizontal plane at 1.2 m)
PCEXTRACTSECTION
(pick the section plane; Optimal, Polylines, layer PC-WALLS, OK)
tools.notes: Extracted geometry is only as good as the scan density; expect to clean it with OVERKILL and JOIN. Not available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: POINTCLOUDMANAGER
tools.description: Opens the Point Cloud Manager palette listing every attached point cloud project with its scans and named regions, each with an on/off toggle and a zoom-to option. It is where individual scans of a multi-scan .rcp are hidden to reduce clutter or to isolate one room. POINTCLOUDMANAGERCLOSE closes it; PCMSTATE reports whether it is open.
tools.usage:
POINTCLOUDMANAGER  (Point Cloud contextual tab > Visibility > Point Cloud Manager)
POINTCLOUDMANAGERCLOSE

parameters.name: Scans
parameters.description: Each .rcs inside the project; toggling visibility is saved with the drawing when POINTCLOUDVISRETAIN is 1.

parameters.name: Regions
parameters.description: Named subsets defined in ReCap; toggle or zoom to them.

tools.example:
POINTCLOUDMANAGER
(uncheck Scan_04 and Scan_05, right-click Level2 region > Zoom To)
tools.notes: Regions are created in ReCap, not in AutoCAD. The manager does not exist for legacy .pcg/.isd clouds from 2014 and earlier.

tools.name: ARCHIVE
tools.description: Packages the current sheet set - every sheet drawing, its xrefs, images, fonts, plot styles and the .dst file - into a ZIP, a self-extracting EXE or a folder, using the same transmittal setups as ETRANSMIT. It is ETRANSMIT for a whole sheet set rather than a single drawing, meant for archiving a project milestone or handing over a complete set. -ARCHIVE is the command-line form used from scripts.
tools.usage:
ARCHIVE  (requires a sheet set open in the Sheet Set Manager)
(Archive a Sheet Set dialog: Sheets / Files Tree / Files Table tabs, Enter notes, Modify Archive Setup, OK -> Save archive dialog)
-ARCHIVE
Enter an option [Create/Report/SEtup] <Create>:

parameters.name: Archive setup
parameters.description: Package type (folder/zip/exe), file format (keep or convert DWG version), path options (keep structure / place all in one folder), include fonts, textures, data links, plot styles, sheet set file, purge and set default plotter to none.

parameters.name: Report
parameters.description: A text file listing every included file and any missing references.

parameters.name: Create
parameters.description: Build the package using the current setup.

tools.example:
OPENSHEETSET C:/proj/1042/1042.dst
-ARCHIVE
C
(accept the current setup; the archive ZIP is written next to the .dst)
tools.notes: Missing references are listed but not fixed - run the report first. ETRANSMIT handles single drawings and can also be run from the Sheet Set Manager on a subset of sheets.

tools.name: GEOGRAPHICLOCATION
tools.description: Assigns a geographic location to the drawing: a latitude/longitude (typed, picked from an online map or read from a KML/KMZ file), a coordinate system (thousands of named GIS coordinate systems, e.g. UTM zones, State Plane, national grids), the drawing point that corresponds to it and the north direction. The geographic marker it places lets GEOMAP show an online map underneath model space, lets point clouds and xrefs with georeferencing attach in the right place, and drives the sun position for rendering. GEOREMOVE strips it all again.
tools.usage:
GEOGRAPHICLOCATION
(Set Location: From Map / From File; Geographic Location dialog: search address, coordinate system list, then in the drawing: Select a point for the location, Specify the north direction angle)
-GEOGRAPHICLOCATION: command-line entry of latitude, longitude, elevation, north
GEOREMOVE  removes location, marker and map

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: Chosen from the list of GIS systems; stored in CGEOCS. Needed for drawing-unit to lat/long conversion.

parameters.name: LATITUDE / LONGITUDE / NORTHDIRECTION
parameters.description: System variables holding the assigned values.

parameters.name: GEOMARKERVISIBILITY
parameters.description: 1 shows the geographic marker glyph in model space.

parameters.name: GEOLATLONGFORMAT
parameters.description: 0 decimal degrees, 1 degrees/minutes/seconds for coordinate display.

tools.example:
GEOGRAPHICLOCATION
(From Map: search 'Munich', drop the marker, Next; pick coordinate system 'ETRS89 / UTM zone 32N', Next)
0,0
90
GEOMAP A (aerial)
tools.notes: Online maps need an Autodesk sign-in and internet access. Map images are for reference and are not plotted at full resolution unless captured with GEOMAPIMAGE. Once a location exists, the Geolocation contextual ribbon tab appears.

tools.name: GEOMAP
tools.description: Displays an online map (Aerial, Road or Hybrid) from the map service in the current model-space viewport, positioned by the drawing's geographic location, or turns it off. The map is a live background that re-tiles as you zoom; to keep a fixed, plottable piece of it use GEOMAPIMAGE, which captures a rectangle into a map image object (updated later with GEOMAPIMAGEUPDATE).
tools.usage:
GEOMAP
Select map type [Aerial/Road/Hybrid/Off] <Aerial>:
GEOMAPIMAGE
Specify first corner: / Specify opposite corner:  (creates a map image object)
GEOMAPIMAGEUPDATE  Select map images: ... [Optimize/Reload]

parameters.name: Aerial / Road / Hybrid / Off
parameters.description: Map style; Off hides the map (GEOMAPMODE 0).

parameters.name: GEOMAPMODE
parameters.description: 0 off, 1 aerial, 2 road, 3 hybrid.

parameters.name: GEOMAPIMAGE resolution
parameters.description: Map image objects carry a Resolution property (Coarse/Optimal/Fine/Very Fine) that sets the captured tile detail.

tools.example:
GEOMAP
H
(zoom to the site)
GEOMAPIMAGE
(two corners around the site)
GEOMAP
Off
tools.notes: The live map does not plot and is not visible in paper space viewports; map images do plot. Requires a location set with GEOGRAPHICLOCATION and an internet connection; tiles are cached locally.

tools.name: GEOMARKPOSITION
tools.description: Places a position marker - a point plus a multiline text label with latitude/longitude or coordinates - at a picked location, by typed latitude/longitude (GEOMARKLATLONG), at a model-space point (GEOMARKPOINT) or at your device's current position (GEOMARKME). Markers are ordinary objects on the current layer, useful for annotating survey points or site photos. GEOREORIENTMARKER changes the geographic marker's north direction and position without changing the location itself.
tools.usage:
GEOMARKPOSITION  Specify a location: <point on the map>  Select a label location:
GEOMARKLATLONG   Enter latitude: / Enter longitude:  Select a label location:
GEOMARKPOINT     Specify a point: (drawing coordinates)
GEOMARKME        (uses the device location service)
GEOREORIENTMARKER  Specify new geographic marker position: / Specify the north direction:

parameters.name: GEOMARKPOSITIONSIZE
parameters.description: Scale factor for the marker's point and text (default 1).

parameters.name: Label
parameters.description: MTEXT with fields for lat/long or XY in the GEOLATLONGFORMAT style; editable like any text.

tools.example:
GEOMARKLATLONG
48.1372
11.5756
(click where the label should sit)
tools.notes: All GEOMARK* commands need a geographic location in the drawing. Markers are not linked to the map; moving one does not update its coordinates text (it is a plain field snapshot).

tools.name: INSERTOBJ
tools.description: Inserts an OLE object - an Excel range, Word document, image or any other OLE server document - either embedded (a copy lives in the DWG) or linked to the source file so it updates. It is the menu-driven form of pasting with PASTESPEC and offers Create New (launch the server) or Create from File. OLE objects display and plot as raster and are managed afterwards with OLELINKS, OLESCALE and the OLEHIDE/OLEQUALITY/OLEFRAME variables.
tools.usage:
INSERTOBJ
(Insert Object dialog: Create New [object type list] or Create from File [Browse, Link checkbox, Display As Icon])

parameters.name: Create New
parameters.description: Start the OLE server application to author a new object in place.

parameters.name: Create from File / Link
parameters.description: Embed a copy, or link to the file so edits in the source appear after OLELINKS > Update.

parameters.name: OLEHIDE
parameters.description: 0 all OLE visible, 1 hidden in paper space, 2 hidden in model space, 3 hidden everywhere.

parameters.name: OLEQUALITY
parameters.description: Plot quality: 0 monochrome, 1 low graphics, 2 high graphics, 3 automatic (default).

parameters.name: MSOLESCALE
parameters.description: Scale factor applied when OLE objects are pasted into model space.

tools.example:
INSERTOBJ
(Create from File, Browse: C:\proj\schedule.xlsx, tick Link, OK)
(place and size the object)
OLELINKS (Update Now when the workbook changes)
tools.notes: Linked Excel tables are fragile (absolute paths, printer-dependent sizing); DATALINK with a TABLE is the native, plot-friendly alternative. OLE objects cannot be rotated and do not appear in DWF/PDF output from some plotters unless OLEQUALITY is set.

tools.name: PASTESPEC
tools.description: Paste Special: pastes the clipboard as a chosen data type instead of AutoCAD's default. For Excel data it offers AutoCAD Entities (creates a native TABLE object, formatting governed by PASTESPECMODE), Picture (Metafile), Bitmap, Text or an OLE link; for text it can paste as MTEXT or as an OLE document. This is the standard way to get a spreadsheet into a drawing as an editable table without a data link.
tools.usage:
PASTESPEC
(Paste Special dialog: Paste / Paste Link; As: AutoCAD Entities, Picture (Metafile), Bitmap, Text, Unicode Text, Microsoft Excel Worksheet ...)
Specify insertion point:

parameters.name: AutoCAD Entities
parameters.description: Excel cells become a TABLE; text becomes MTEXT; metafile geometry becomes lines/polylines/text.

parameters.name: Paste Link
parameters.description: Create an OLE link that updates from the source file.

parameters.name: PASTESPECMODE
parameters.description: 2023+: 0 keeps Excel cell formatting in the table, 1 uses the current table style only.

tools.example:
(copy A1:F20 in Excel)
PASTESPEC
(choose AutoCAD Entities, OK)
0,0
tools.notes: A pasted table has no link; to keep it synchronised use DATALINK + TABLE. Large ranges paste slowly; copy values rather than formulas.

tools.name: COPYBASE
tools.description: Copies selected objects to the Windows clipboard with a base point you specify, so that pasting into another drawing (PASTECLIP) lets you place them precisely instead of by the lower-left corner of their extents. CUTBASE (2023+) does the same and removes the originals. It is the pair to PASTEBLOCK and PASTEORIG for moving geometry between drawings exactly.
tools.usage:
COPYBASE  (Ctrl+Shift+C)
Specify base point: <point>
Select objects: <selection> Enter
CUTBASE  (Ctrl+Shift+X) same prompts, originals erased

parameters.name: base point
parameters.description: The point that will sit at the insertion point when pasted.

parameters.name: PASTECLIP (Ctrl+V)
parameters.description: Paste at a picked point; objects keep their layers, creating them if missing.

parameters.name: PASTEORIG
parameters.description: Paste at the same coordinates as the source drawing - no point prompt; only enabled when pasting into a different drawing.

tools.example:
; in drawing A
COPYBASE
0,0
(select the grid) Enter
; in drawing B
PASTEORIG   (lands at the same coordinates)
; or
PASTECLIP
1000,500
tools.notes: COPYCLIP (Ctrl+C) uses the lower-left of the extents as base. Clipboard data includes a DWG stream, so pasting into Word or Excel gives an OLE picture of the objects. Clipboard operations are unavailable in the Core Console.

tools.name: COPYCLIP
tools.description: Copies selected objects to the Windows clipboard (Ctrl+C) in AutoCAD, metafile, bitmap and text formats; CUTCLIP (Ctrl+X) copies and erases; PASTECLIP (Ctrl+V) pastes AutoCAD objects at a picked point or, for foreign content, inserts an OLE object or text. Objects are pasted onto their original layers (created if necessary) and keep their properties, and when pasted into the same drawing the base point is the extents corner unless COPYBASE was used.
tools.usage:
COPYCLIP   Select objects: <selection> Enter
CUTCLIP    Select objects: <selection> Enter
PASTECLIP  Specify insertion point: <point>

parameters.name: Clipboard formats
parameters.description: AutoCAD (DWG stream), Picture (Metafile), Bitmap and Text; PASTESPEC chooses among them.

parameters.name: PASTEBLOCK
parameters.description: Paste the clipboard as a single anonymous block instead of loose objects.

parameters.name: WMFBKGND / WMFFOREGND
parameters.description: Control background/foreground colours of the metafile copied for other applications.

tools.example:
COPYCLIP
(select the legend) Enter
(switch to the other drawing)
PASTECLIP
(click in the layout)
tools.notes: Pasting between drawings with different INSUNITS scales the objects according to the unit ratio (INSUNITSDEFSOURCE/TARGET govern unitless files). Annotative objects paste with their scales. The DIVIDE/MEASURE and dimension associativity are not preserved across drawings.

tools.name: PASTEBLOCK
tools.description: Pastes the AutoCAD objects on the clipboard as a single block reference with an anonymous definition (named A$C...), so a group of objects can be placed, moved and rotated as one unit and later exploded. Combine with COPYBASE to control the block's insertion point. PASTEASHYPERLINK pastes text as a hyperlink attached to a selected object instead.
tools.usage:
PASTEBLOCK  (Ctrl+Shift+V)
Specify insertion point: <point>
PASTEASHYPERLINK
Select objects: <objects to receive the hyperlink>

parameters.name: insertion point
parameters.description: The base point from COPYBASE or the extents corner from COPYCLIP.

parameters.name: anonymous block
parameters.description: Definition named A$C<hex>; rename with RENAME or BEDIT > Save Block As if it should become a library block.

tools.example:
COPYBASE 0,0 (select the north arrow objects)
PASTEBLOCK
2500,1800
RENAME B A$C3F2A1B04 NORTH_ARROW
tools.notes: Anonymous blocks are purged automatically when unreferenced. PASTEBLOCK is also the quickest way to group xref-derived geometry before scaling.

tools.name: HYPERLINK
tools.description: Attaches, edits or removes a hyperlink on selected objects: a URL, a file (optionally with a named view or layout as the target), or an e-mail address. Hovering an object with a link shows the hyperlink cursor and Ctrl+click opens it; links survive into PDF and DWF output when the plot driver includes hyperlinks. -HYPERLINK is the command-line form and HYPERLINKBASE sets a base path so relative links resolve.
tools.usage:
HYPERLINK  (Ctrl+K)
Select objects: <selection> Enter
(Insert Hyperlink dialog: Existing File or Web Page / View of This Drawing / E-mail Address; Text to display; Target)
-HYPERLINK
Enter an option [Remove/Insert] <Insert>:
Enter hyperlink insert option [Area/Object] <Object>:

parameters.name: Text to display
parameters.description: Tooltip shown on hover (defaults to the URL).

parameters.name: Target / View
parameters.description: A named view or layout in the linked DWG.

parameters.name: Area (in -HYPERLINK)
parameters.description: Create a rectangular hyperlink area (a URLLAYER polyline) instead of attaching to objects.

parameters.name: HYPERLINKBASE
parameters.description: System variable: base path or URL prepended to relative hyperlinks in this drawing.

parameters.name: PICKFIRST / HYPERLINKOPTIONS
parameters.description: HYPERLINKOPTIONS toggles the cursor, tooltip and shortcut-menu display of hyperlinks.

tools.example:
-HYPERLINK
I
O
(select the detail bubble) Enter
Details.dwg#Detail_5
Open detail 5

; Express Tools SHOWURLS lists every hyperlink; CHURLS / REPURLS edit them
tools.notes: Hyperlinks are stored as xdata (PE_URL), so they are preserved through copy/paste and WBLOCK. Block references can carry a link separate from the links inside the definition.

tools.name: CLIPIT
tools.description: Express Tool that clips an xref, block or raster image with a curved boundary - a polyline with arcs, a circle, an ellipse or a spline - by approximating the curve with many short segments. XCLIP and IMAGECLIP only accept polygons of straight segments, so CLIPIT is the way to show a circular detail of a site plan xref or a rounded photo.
tools.usage:
CLIPIT
Pick a POLYLINE, CIRCLE, ARC, ELLIPSE, or TEXT object for clipping edge...
Select objects: <the boundary object>
Pick an IMAGE, a WIPEOUT, or an XREF/BLOCK to clip...
Select objects: <the reference>
Enter maximum allowable error distance for resolution of arc segments <0.02>:

parameters.name: error distance
parameters.description: Chord tolerance for approximating arcs; smaller = more segments = smoother edge but slower.

tools.example:
CIRCLE 5000,5000 800
CLIPIT
(select the circle)
(select the site xref)
5
tools.notes: The boundary object is left in the drawing; erase it afterwards. Very small tolerances can create thousands of vertices and slow regeneration. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: DATALINKUPDATE
tools.description: Synchronises tables that are linked to external Excel data (DATALINK): downloads changes from the spreadsheet into the drawing tables, or uploads edits made in the tables back to the workbook, for all links or a selection. It is what the 'Data link has changed' balloon runs and what a script calls before plotting so schedules are current.
tools.usage:
DATALINKUPDATE
Select an option [Update data link/Write data link] <Update data link>:
Select objects or [Data link/All]: <tables> | D name | A

parameters.name: Update data link
parameters.description: Pull the current spreadsheet contents into the table(s).

parameters.name: Write data link
parameters.description: Push cell edits from the table(s) to the spreadsheet; only allowed if the link permits writing.

parameters.name: Data link (D) / All (A)
parameters.description: Choose links by name, or refresh every link in the drawing.

parameters.name: DATALINKNOTIFY
parameters.description: 0 no notification, 1 balloon, 2 balloon plus status-bar icon when the source changes.

tools.example:
; Script prelude before publishing
DATALINKUPDATE
U
A

; AutoLISP
(command "_.DATALINKUPDATE" "_U" "_A")
tools.notes: Locked cells in a linked table (the default for data cells) are only editable after unlocking; writing back needs Excel installed. Data links use absolute paths unless created as relative in the Data Link Manager.

tools.name: VISRETAIN
tools.description: Controls whether xref-dependent layer settings (on/off, freeze, colour, linetype, lineweight, plot style, transparency) changed in the host drawing are kept when the drawing is reopened or the xref reloaded (1, default) or reset to the xref file's own settings each time (0). Since 2018.1 VISRETAINMODE refines which properties are synchronised when VISRETAIN is 1, and XREFOVERRIDE forces all xref objects to display ByLayer.
tools.usage:
VISRETAIN = 0 | 1
VISRETAINMODE = bit sum (0 keep all host overrides; 1 sync On/Off, 2 Freeze/Thaw, 4 Color, 8 Linetype, 16 Lineweight, 32 Plot style, 64 Transparency, 128 New layers from the xref are set as in the xref)
XREFOVERRIDE = 0 | 1 | 2

parameters.name: VISRETAIN 1
parameters.description: Host overrides win; xref layer changes made in the source file are ignored unless VISRETAINMODE syncs that property.

parameters.name: VISRETAIN 0
parameters.description: Xref file settings win on every load; host overrides are discarded.

parameters.name: XREFOVERRIDE
parameters.description: 0 xref objects keep their own properties, 1 treat all xref objects as ByLayer (colour/linetype/lineweight from the xref layer), 2 like 1 plus the properties of xref layers follow the host's layer of the same name.

tools.example:
VISRETAIN 1
VISRETAINMODE 3     ; keep colours/linetypes from the host but follow the xref's on/off and freeze state
XREFOVERRIDE 1      ; show every xref object ByLayer so the whole background can be greyed via layers
tools.notes: Saved in the drawing. A common cause of 'my xref layer colours keep coming back' is VISRETAIN 0 in the host. XREFOVERRIDE 1 is the quickest way to make a consultant's drawing plot grey without editing it.

tools.name: XLOADCTL
tools.description: Sets demand loading of xrefs: 0 loads whole xref files and keeps them open, 1 demand-loads only the visible/needed parts and locks the file, 2 (default) demand-loads from a temporary copy (in XLOADPATH) so other users can still edit the source. Demand loading with spatial and layer indexes (INDEXCTL in the xref file) makes clipped, layer-frozen xrefs of huge drawings fast.
tools.usage:
XLOADCTL = 0 | 1 | 2
XLOADPATH = folder for the temporary copies used when XLOADCTL is 2
INDEXCTL (set in the referenced drawing) = 0 none, 1 layer index, 2 spatial index, 3 both

parameters.description: No demand loading; the entire xref is loaded.
Demand loading, source file locked while referenced.
Demand loading from a copy; source stays editable (default).

tools.example:
XLOADCTL 2
XLOADPATH C:\Temp\xrefcopies
; in the large background drawing:
INDEXCTL 3
QSAVE
tools.notes: Registry setting, not per drawing. XLOADCTL 1 is the usual reason a colleague cannot save a drawing that someone else has xref'd. Layer indexes only help when layers are frozen in the host and the xref was saved with the index.

tools.name: REFPATHTYPE
tools.description: Sets the default path type used when a new xref, image, underlay or point cloud is attached (2018+): 0 no path (file name only, resolved through the support search path and the host folder), 1 relative path (default) or 2 full/absolute path. Relative paths are what keep project sets portable, and this variable makes them the default without changing the dialog each time.
tools.usage: REFPATHTYPE = 0 (No path) | 1 (Relative, default) | 2 (Full path)

parameters.name: 0 No path
parameters.description: Only the file name is stored; AutoCAD searches the host drawing folder, then the support paths and the project paths (PROJECTNAME).

parameters.name: 1 Relative
parameters.description: Stored as ..\xrefs\SITE.dwg relative to the host; the host must be saved first, and references on another drive fall back to full path.

parameters.name: 2 Full path
parameters.description: Absolute path; breaks when the folder moves.

tools.example:
REFPATHTYPE 1
-XREF A C:/proj/1042/xrefs/SITE.dwg 0,0 1 1 0
(the saved path shows as .\xrefs\SITE.dwg)
tools.notes: Only affects new attachments; use the External References palette's Change Path Type for existing ones. Before 2018 the dialog default was full path and PROJECTNAME-based search paths were the portability mechanism.

tools.name: XDWGFADECTL
tools.description: Fades the display of DWG xrefs by a percentage so the host drawing stands out (default 70 in recent releases). It affects the screen only, never plots, and applies to all xrefs at once; PDF/DWF/DGN underlays are faded individually with ADJUST and images with IMAGEADJUST. XFADECTL is the separate fade applied to non-working-set objects during REFEDIT.
tools.usage:
XDWGFADECTL = -90 .. 90  (positive fades, negative stores the value while fading is off; 0 no fade)
XFADECTL = 0 .. 90  (fade of objects outside the REFEDIT working set)

parameters.name: value > 0
parameters.description: Percentage of fading applied to xref objects on screen.

parameters.name: value < 0
parameters.description: Fading turned off but the magnitude remembered; the Options > Display slider toggles the sign.

tools.example:
XDWGFADECTL 50
; turn off without losing the setting
XDWGFADECTL -50
tools.notes: Registry setting. Fading is not applied to xrefs in the Core Console or to plots; to plot xrefs grey use XREFOVERRIDE with grey layers or a CTB screening.
